paragraphs: A reasoning model can spend substantial computation on questions that a cheaper model could answer adequately. Routing some questions to a model that skips extended reasoning can save work, but deciding when to do so is difficult online. The consequences of routing decisions are only partly observed, and the incoming data can change over time.

B-PAC reasoning adjusts its routing threshold using accumulated statistical evidence about performance loss. It uses inverse propensity scoring to account for partial feedback and constructs test supermartingales for candidate thresholds. These statistical tools support checks that remain valid as evidence accumulates, allowing the system to keep updating its routing decisions.

The paper establishes theoretical guarantees for anytime-valid performance-loss control and efficiency. Experiments report reductions in thinking-model usage of up to 81.01%, while keeping performance loss below a user-selected level. The contribution is a way to make computation savings responsive to measured risk throughout online operation, with safety referring specifically to controlled performance loss.
icml-2026-anytime-safe-pac-efficient-rea.tldr: B-PAC routes queries between thinking and non-thinking models using statistical evidence to reduce computation while controlling performance loss over time.

paragraphs: Choosing transistor sizes in analog and mixed-signal circuits requires navigating nonlinear behavior, many interacting design variables, and strict performance requirements. Conventional optimization methods often treat the search space as fixed. AutoSizer addresses the possibility that the search itself needs to change as simulations reveal which constraints and design choices matter.

The framework gives an LLM responsibility for understanding the circuit and directing optimization. An inner loop performs circuit sizing, while an outer loop examines optimization behavior and simulation feedback to refine the search space. This division uses the language model to organize and adapt the numerical search, addressing the abstract’s observation that LLMs are poorly suited to precise numerical optimization themselves.

The paper also introduces AMS-SizingBench, containing 24 circuits in SKY130 CMOS technology for evaluating adaptive optimization under simulator-based constraints. Experiments report better solution quality, faster convergence, and higher success rates than traditional optimizers and existing LLM agents across varying circuit difficulties. These findings support adapting the search strategy as part of circuit sizing.
icml-2026-autosizer-automatic-sizing-of-.tldr: AutoSizer uses an LLM to repeatedly refine circuit-sizing searches from simulation feedback, improving experimental optimization outcomes.

paragraphs: Alignment connects corresponding elements across sources, such as networks, modalities, or point clouds. Optimal transport provides a framework for aligning distributions, but its effectiveness can depend on a small amount of expensive supervision. AvAtar addresses the question of which additional supervision would be most informative for the overall alignment.

It scores a candidate by tracing how its possible supervision would affect the global alignment result through an entropy-regularized optimal transport formulation. This gradient-based view connects a local request for information to its potential effect on the whole problem. Because differentiating through constrained optimal transport is difficult, the method uses an adjoint-state reformulation that produces a linear system.

That system is solved with conjugate gradients, with linear complexity and guaranteed convergence as stated in the abstract. Utility functions express the desired global alignment outcome, allowing the framework to accommodate different alignment problems. Experiments on three representative tasks support its effectiveness, scalability, and generalizability. The central contribution is making supervision acquisition an explicit part of optimal transport alignment.
icml-2026-avatar-learning-to-align-via-a.tldr: AvAtar selects informative alignment supervision by efficiently estimating its gradient-based effect on an optimal transport solution.

paragraphs: Symbolic regression searches for formulas that explain data, usually balancing predictive accuracy against expression size. The paper argues that a compact, accurate formula can still have an unstable or physically difficult-to-explain structure. It introduces the Effective Information Criterion, or EIC, to evaluate a property that those two objectives can miss.

EIC treats a formula as an information channel and measures how rounding noise is amplified as its calculations unfold. This provides a structural assessment without requiring a known correct formula. The analysis finds a substantial stability gap between human-derived equations and symbolic-regression outputs. EIC then supplies guidance during heuristic search and a filtering criterion for data used to train generative models.

The reported benefits include improved accuracy–complexity trade-offs in heuristic search, two- to fourfold better pretraining sample efficiency, and a 22.4% improvement in generalization R² for generative models. In a study involving 108 experts, EIC agrees with human preferences in 70% of cases. These results support structural stability as a useful additional dimension of formula assessment.
icml-2026-beyond-accuracy-and-complexity.tldr: EIC evaluates how formulas amplify rounding noise, helping symbolic regression favor structurally stable expressions alongside accuracy and simplicity.

paragraphs: Tracking text through video presents difficulties that general object trackers do not handle well. Perspective changes can severely distort characters, different text instances can look similar, and small structural details matter. The paper formalizes scene text tracking as a dedicated task, motivated by applications including text segmentation, removal, and editing across frames.

Its proposed framework, SymTrack, uses a detection-free design with two cooperating branches. Cross-Expert Calibration addresses semantic bias, Predictive Token Rectification corrects structural imbalances, and an Adaptive Inference Engine stabilizes predictions using motion constraints. Together, these components address both what makes a text instance distinctive and how its appearance and position evolve through a video.

The authors construct evaluation benchmarks from three video text spotting datasets with high-quality annotations. SymTrack achieves the best reported performance on all three, with an improvement of up to 11.97% AUC over previous best trackers on BOVText_SOT. These findings support treating text structure explicitly when developing trackers for video text manipulation.
icml-2026-beyond-detection-a-structure-a.tldr: SymTrack combines text-structure modeling and motion-aware inference to improve scene text tracking across three benchmarks.

paragraphs: Custom gesture recognition must accommodate movements chosen for a particular interaction while keeping training data requirements manageable. For intelligent devices, model size also matters. This paper targets the combined challenge of recognizing gestures accurately, learning from few examples, and limiting the number of parameters needed by the recognition system.

The proposed framework combines an IMU-based recognition model called BiCrossNet with two data augmentation models, named the delta-generator and embedding-generator. The recognition model and augmentation components address the learning problem together: the system seeks better recognition under limited examples while reducing the size of its pretrained feature extractor. Its intended application is touchless control through hand or body movements.

Compared with existing methods, the abstract reports accuracy improvements of 11.7% and 12.7% on the public UMAHand dataset, and 8.85% and 5.25% on the authors’ GRHand dataset. It also reports 27.8% fewer pretrained feature-extractor parameters. These results indicate a favorable experimental balance between recognition performance and model size, supporting the framework’s intended use on intelligent terminal devices.
icml-2026-bicrossnet-with-decoupled-dual.tldr: BiCrossNet combines IMU-based gesture recognition with two augmentation models, reporting higher accuracy with fewer feature-extractor parameters.

paragraphs: A vision-language model can produce plausible reasoning while relying too heavily on familiar language patterns and too little on the image. The paper identifies this grounding failure, including drift during long reasoning chains, as a problem with reinforcement learning approaches that lack explicit mechanisms for counterfactual and causal learning.

Counterfactual Policy Optimization, or CFPO, trains with a comparison between the original visual input and a counterfactual state in which critical visual cues are suppressed. Its regularization objective increases the discrepancy between predictions in these two states. The intended effect is to make the model’s reasoning depend more strongly on visual evidence that should matter to the answer.

CFPO integrates with GRPO and DAPO without external reward models or additional supervision. Experiments report consistent gains of 3.17%–6.25% over standard reinforcement learning baselines and 1.32%–2.13% over the perception-aware method PAPO. These results support counterfactual visual interventions as a practical training mechanism for improving reasoning fidelity in the evaluated vision-language models.
icml-2026-cfpo-counterfactual-policy-opt.tldr: CFPO improves multimodal reasoning by training models to respond differently when critical visual evidence is removed.

paragraphs: Adding more rounds of collaboration to a visual multi-agent system does not necessarily improve its answers. The paper reports an empirical pattern in which performance can decline while token costs rise exponentially. It attributes this problem to text-based communication compressing perceptual information and reasoning trajectories into language, with associated loss of meaning.

L²-VMAS introduces two latent memories to support collaboration while separating perception from thinking. The framework dynamically synthesizes these memories, giving agents a different means of sharing information. It also uses an entropy-driven trigger for proactive memory access, so information is accessed on demand rather than transmitted passively throughout the interaction.

Experiments cover different model backbones, model sizes, and multi-agent arrangements. The reported results show average accuracy improvements of 2.7%–5.4% alongside reductions in total token usage of 21.3%–44.8%. Within those experiments, the method overcomes the observed deterioration from additional collaboration. The findings connect effective scaling to how agents preserve and access information, as well as to the number of interaction rounds.
icml-2026-dual-latent-memory-for-visual-.tldr: L²-VMAS separates perceptual and reasoning memories to improve visual multi-agent collaboration while reducing token use.

paragraphs: Mixture-of-experts upcycling expands a pretrained model by replicating existing networks, helping it learn new tasks while retaining earlier knowledge. The paper argues that expanding capacity indiscriminately creates redundant parameters. It investigates where expansion is useful by studying representation similarity with Centered Kernel Alignment, or CKA, together with loss-landscape flatness.

The analysis finds unstable representations in deeper layers and differences in how sensitive individual experts are to new tasks. These observations motivate selective growth. An outer optimization loop uses a differentiable Gumbel-Softmax mask to search for an appropriate expansion pattern. An inner loop updates model weights using task objectives and replay regularized by CKA.

On the TRACE benchmark, the framework achieves better average accuracy and reports an 80% reduction in forgetting. It also removes 60% of the redundant parameter expansion that standard upcycling would introduce. The results support coordinating architectural growth with representation-preserving training, so additional capacity is allocated according to the model’s differing needs across its structure.
icml-2026-efficient-bilevel-optimization.tldr: This method selectively expands mixture-of-experts models using bilevel optimization, reducing forgetting and redundant growth on TRACE.

paragraphs: Multi-fidelity regression combines observations of differing quality, often with many low-fidelity examples and very few high-fidelity ones. Common Gaussian-process approaches can become expensive as data grows and can overfit the scarce high-quality observations. FIRE addresses this imbalance using pretrained tabular foundation models without retraining them for the regression task.

The framework connects a low-fidelity predictor to a high-fidelity correction model through predictive distributions. Passing distributional summaries gives the correction model information about uncertainty as well as predicted values. This supports learning residual corrections when error levels vary across inputs. The models perform Bayesian inference through examples supplied in context, making cross-fidelity transfer part of inference itself.

Across 31 synthetic and real-world benchmark problems, FIRE ranks highest in accuracy and uncertainty quantification among the seven compared methods, while offering runtime advantages. The results support its reported performance–time trade-off. Its applicability remains constrained by the models’ context windows and by the quality of the pretrained tabular foundation models, both limitations explicitly identified in the abstract.
icml-2026-fire-multi-fidelity-regression.tldr: FIRE transfers predictive distributions between tabular foundation models to perform accurate, uncertainty-aware multi-fidelity regression without retraining.

paragraphs: Federated graph learning lets clients collaborate on graph representations while preserving the privacy of their graph data. Collaboration becomes harder when clients differ in both node features and connection patterns. FedSSA addresses these two sources of heterogeneity separately, aligning semantic information and structural information within a shared learning framework.

For node features, a variational model estimates class-specific node distributions. Clients are grouped according to these distributions, and each client’s local distributions are aligned with representatives of its cluster. For graph structure, the method uses spectral graph neural networks and a spectral energy measure to characterize topology. This supports alignment between local and cluster-level spectral models.

Experiments evaluate eleven datasets covering homophilic and heterophilic graphs, with both overlapping and non-overlapping client partitions. FedSSA consistently outperforms eleven compared state-of-the-art methods in those evaluations. The findings support organizing knowledge sharing around differences among clients, using distribution-based grouping for node information and a separate structural alignment mechanism for graph topology.
icml-2026-heterogeneity-aware-knowledge-.tldr: FedSSA improves federated graph learning by aligning client groups separately on node-feature distributions and graph structure.

paragraphs: HiPhO evaluates language and multimodal models using high school physics Olympiad exams, with scoring designed to support comparison with human contestants. It collects 13 competitions from 2024–2025, including international and regional events. The problems span text-only questions and questions requiring diagrams, making the benchmark relevant to both textual and visual physics reasoning.

The evaluation follows official grading rubrics at the answer and reasoning-step levels. It then assigns models gold, silver, or bronze medals using the competitions’ official score thresholds. This gives performance a concrete interpretation tied to existing human examinations, while step-level grading provides more detail than checking only whether a final answer is correct.

Across 30 models and 13 exams, most open-source multimodal models reach bronze level or below. Open-source language models earn multiple gold medals, while closed-source multimodal models earn between 6 and 13. Most models nevertheless remain well below full marks. The results show substantial progress alongside the reported gap between evaluated models and top human contestants.
icml-2026-hipho-how-far-are-m-llms-from-.tldr: HiPhO uses official physics Olympiad grading and medal thresholds to compare 30 models with human contestants.

paragraphs: Online optimization studies decisions made over a sequence of changing losses. With bandit feedback, the learner sees limited evaluations rather than complete information about each loss function. This paper develops guarantees that reflect gradient variation, allowing the analysis to account for how the optimization problem changes across the sequence.

The main contribution is a refined treatment of non-consecutive gradient variation in bandit convex optimization with two-point feedback. It improves how the guarantees depend on dimension for both convex and strongly convex losses compared with the previous best results. The same analysis also produces guarantees expressed through gradient variance and small loss, connecting performance to additional properties of the particular problem.

The technique extends beyond this setting. The paper establishes the first gradient-variation guarantee for one-point bandit linear optimization over hyper-rectangular domains. It also derives the first gradient-variation bounds for dynamic and universal regret in two-point bandit convex optimization. These are theoretical advances in making limited-feedback guarantees more responsive to problem structure.
icml-2026-improved-dimension-dependence-.tldr: A refined gradient-variation analysis improves dimension dependence and extends problem-dependent guarantees in bandit optimization.

paragraphs: LiDAR NeRFs can synthesize static environments well, but moving objects create conflicting information across frames. Early motion estimates can be unreliable, making it difficult to distinguish actual geometry from motion-related errors. MAC-NeRF organizes learning as a curriculum so that the model begins with more trustworthy information before addressing harder motion.

Its Rectified Temporal Consistency component checks geometric correspondences in both forward and backward directions. This filters erroneous supervision and prioritizes reliable temporal matches. A second component, Confidence-Modulated Frequency Regularization, controls how much geometric detail the model can represent during learning. It starts with strong low-frequency constraints to suppress artifacts, then progressively allows a wider frequency range to preserve fine detail.

These components coordinate the reliability of supervision with the complexity of the geometry being learned. Experiments on KITTI-360 and nuScenes report significantly better rendering quality than state-of-the-art methods. The findings support a staged approach to dynamic scene synthesis, where difficult motion and detailed geometry are introduced as the training process becomes better able to handle them.
icml-2026-mac-nerf-motion-aware-curricul.tldr: MAC-NeRF improves dynamic LiDAR scene synthesis by gradually introducing harder motion supervision and finer geometric detail.

paragraphs: Image-to-video diffusion models use a reference image to guide video generation. That input also provides an entry point for adversarial noise. The paper studies attacks intended to suppress motion, observing that conventional frame-level attacks tend to create superficial visual artifacts without overcoming the models’ strong learned temporal behavior.

The authors connect static generated video to a collapse in the rank of the temporal attention matrix, specifically a rank-one degenerate state. MEDUSA targets this behavior by minimizing the matrix’s nuclear norm. This spectral objective is designed to induce temporal rank collapse and freeze generated motion, focusing the attack on the structure of temporal attention.

The paper also analyzes why directly imposing a rigid temporal mapping can lead to vanishing gradients, and explains how its objective avoids that optimization problem. Experiments report strong motion-elimination performance and support the effectiveness of spectral constraints. The contribution combines an account of motion failure inside the model with an attack objective built around that account.
icml-2026-medusa-motion-elimination-in-d.tldr: MEDUSA suppresses generated video motion by using a spectral attack to collapse the rank of temporal attention.

paragraphs: Rewarding a model for correct answers can improve accuracy without ensuring that its written reasoning explains how it reached those answers. This paper examines that distinction for reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards. It asks whether reasoning tokens affect the answer and whether the reasoning itself gives a verifier enough information to determine an unambiguous answer.

The authors introduce Causal Importance of Reasoning to measure the cumulative effect of reasoning tokens on the final answer. Sufficiency of Reasoning measures whether a verifier can recover an unambiguous answer from the reasoning alone. Experiments with Qwen2.5 models on ReasoningGym find that outcome-based reinforcement learning improves task accuracy but does not reliably improve either measure.

Two training modifications help in the reported experiments. A small amount of supervised fine-tuning before reinforcement learning can improve both properties. Alternatively, auxiliary rewards targeting the two measures improve reasoning without that supervised stage, while matching ordinary outcome-reward training accuracy. The findings show why answer correctness and the usefulness of a reasoning trace require separate assessment.
icml-2026-outcome-rewards-do-not-guarant.tldr: Correct-answer rewards do not reliably make reasoning causally important or sufficient, but targeted training changes improve both in the studied settings.

paragraphs: Regions with high curvature contain important geometric detail in a 3D point cloud, but they are relatively sparse. A representation dominated by abundant smooth regions can obscure those details. The paper connects this difficulty to the limited room available for separating intricate features within a uniform-scale Euclidean feature space.

PointCHR introduces curvature-aware hyperbolic rectification to redistribute representational capacity. Its learnable mechanism uses curvature to adjust points’ radial positions in a hyperbolic representation. High-curvature points are projected toward boundary regions with greater effective embedding capacity. The method draws on the exponential volume expansion of hyperbolic geometry to reduce crowding among features that need more room to remain distinguishable.

Experiments report that PointCHR significantly improves the ability of backbone networks to capture fine geometric details and achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks. The contribution is a geometry-based way to address imbalance in which parts of a point cloud receive expressive representation, allocating more capacity to sparse regions that carry important local shape information.
icml-2026-pointchr-point-cloud-analysis-.tldr: PointCHR uses curvature-guided hyperbolic embeddings to give sparse, detailed point-cloud regions more representational capacity.

paragraphs: During supervised fine-tuning, weighting individual tokens determines where a model spends its learning effort. The probability assigned to the correct token indicates alignment with the target, while prediction entropy describes uncertainty. The paper argues that either signal alone can misallocate effort by overlooking the other aspect of a prediction.

RankTuner combines these perspectives through a Relative Rank Indicator. It compares the correct token’s rank with the expected rank under the model’s predicted distribution. The inverse of this indicator becomes a token-specific scale on the training objective. This calibration is intended to emphasize tokens that are under-learned while avoiding excessive penalties at positions where uncertainty is intrinsic.

Experiments across multiple model backbones report consistent improvements on mathematical reasoning benchmarks and transfer gains on reasoning outside the training distribution. The abstract also reports better code-generation performance than probability-only or entropy-only weighting baselines. These findings support evaluating a target token relative to the surrounding predictive distribution when deciding how strongly it should influence a fine-tuning update.
icml-2026-probability-entropy-calibratio.tldr: RankTuner calibrates token-level fine-tuning weights using the correct token’s rank relative to the model’s predictive distribution.

paragraphs: Rephrasing existing web text can expand useful pretraining material, but the rewritten text needs to retain the source’s important information. RePro trains a relatively small language model specifically for this task. Its reinforcement learning objective combines one quality reward with three faithfulness rewards to improve rephrasings while preserving core meaning and structure.

The study trains a rephraser with as few as one billion parameters and applies it to 72 billion tokens sampled from DCLM-RefinedWeb. Models with 400 million, 1.4 billion, and 2.8 billion parameters are then pretrained to evaluate the resulting data. This tests the value of the rewritten material through downstream model performance.

Across 22 downstream tasks, RePro yields relative accuracy gains of 3.7%–14.5% over training only on organic data, doubling the gains of a prompting-based method using a 70-billion-parameter rephraser. Experiments also report two- to threefold better organic-data efficiency. Individual and distributional analyses find stronger preservation of critical information and source-data characteristics, supporting explicit faithfulness training for web recycling.
icml-2026-repro-training-language-models.tldr: RePro trains a small rephrasing model with quality and faithfulness rewards to turn existing web text into more effective pretraining data.

paragraphs: Scientific reasoning requires valid connections between steps, as well as a correct final answer. This paper examines that internal logicality in language-model reasoning. It argues that expanding training datasets and lengthening reasoning chains can overlook the logical structure that makes a scientific conclusion follow from the preceding work.

The authors develop assessment criteria and data-sampling methods that make logicality an explicit consideration in training. They apply the methodology to physics because the discipline contains varied logical structures and formalisms. Scientific problems are extracted from academic literature, and the sampling process constructs a high-quality dataset selected for strong logicality.

Experiments with three different backbone language models find that training on this dataset improves the scientific logicality of their reasoning. The results also indicate that improved logicality plays an important role in solving scientific problems. The contribution links the assessment of reasoning quality to the construction of training data, supporting a route toward better logical faithfulness and task performance in the studied physics setting.
icml-2026-scientific-logicality-enriched.tldr: This work uses logicality assessment and data selection to improve language models’ scientific reasoning, demonstrated through physics.

paragraphs: Shape from polarization estimates surface orientation from polarization images. Ice makes this difficult because its light–matter interactions produce a nonlinear relationship between observed polarization and surface normals. This paper uses ice as a representative complex medium and develops a method that incorporates local spatial structure into the estimation process.

The method constructs a prior from autocorrelation functions to describe local consistency in the angle of linear polarization. A dual-branch network called IceSfP combines that prior with raw polarization features. Cross-modal attention and feature fusion at multiple scales allow the two sources of information to contribute jointly to surface-normal estimates from a single view.

The authors also construct the first real-world ice dataset for this task. Experiments report improvements over existing approaches on every evaluated metric, including a mean angular error of 16.01 degrees, 2.74 degrees below the second-best method. These findings support using spatial consistency alongside raw polarization measurements for geometric perception in ice, the complex medium directly studied.
icml-2026-structure-aware-consistency-pr.tldr: IceSfP combines raw polarization measurements with local consistency priors to improve surface-normal estimation on a new real-world ice dataset.

paragraphs: Long-context language models repeatedly process a growing cache of keys and values during decoding, making attention expensive. Sparse attention reduces this work by selecting fewer cache entries, but selection can introduce accuracy loss or its own training and computational costs. BinaryPC addresses the selection problem with compact, data-aware binary hashes.

The method computes binary principal components to construct both hash codes and their corresponding hash function. These codes are designed to preserve structural information in the data without gradient-based training. The approach therefore adapts its hashing to the observed data, giving the sparse attention mechanism a structured basis for selecting relevant key-value pairs.

Experiments across multiple model families and long-context benchmarks report preserved accuracy relative to full attention and stronger performance than the compared sparse and hashing-based alternatives. On modern GPUs, the reported end-to-end decoding throughput is 3.56 times that of the FlashAttention kernel. The findings support binary principal components as a practical route to reducing attention work while retaining accuracy in the evaluated settings.
icml-2026-training-free-hashing-based-at.tldr: BinaryPC uses data-aware binary hashing to accelerate long-context attention without additional training, preserving accuracy in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Three-dimensional reasoning segmentation identifies objects in a 3D scene from text instructions and spatial information. Multimodal language models offer useful semantic abilities, but their training on text-image pairs does not transfer straightforwardly to unstructured point clouds. TVDRNet addresses this mismatch by learning which rendered views make the requested object easier to identify.

A differentiable renderer lets text supervision guide adjustments to intrinsic and extrinsic rendering parameters. This creates task-relevant 2D images that the multimodal model can process. The AVPL module learns the connection between instruction meaning and rendering parameters, while the MGL module combines modalities through semantic grouping to guide the generation of object masks.

The approach makes viewpoint selection part of interpreting the instruction: where the system looks depends on what it has been asked to find. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance on the Reason3D and Instruct3D reasoning-segmentation benchmarks and the ScanRefer visual-grounding benchmark. These findings support optimizing the visual presentation of a 3D scene for the language-guided task.
icml-2026-tvdrnet-text-driven-viewpoint-.tldr: TVDRNet learns text-guided camera views that help multimodal models locate and segment requested objects in 3D scenes.

paragraphs: Large neural networks can generalize well even when their parameter counts suggest substantial capacity to overfit. This paper studies a fixed, already-trained model through the geometry of its learned embeddings. Its goal is to explain the gap between performance on held-out examples and performance over the underlying population.

The derived bound depends on two ingredients. The intrinsic dimension of the embedding determines how quickly its empirical distribution approaches the population distribution in Wasserstein distance. Lipschitz constants describe how sensitive the downstream prediction mapping is to changes in those embeddings. Together, these connect the representation’s distributional behavior to the model’s generalization gap.

At the final embedding layer, the architectural sensitivity contribution disappears, leaving embedding dimension as the dominant part of the bound. This provides a post-training explanation for the strong empirical association between embedding dimension and generalization. Experiments across architectures and datasets support the theory and the usefulness of embedding-based diagnostics. The analysis concerns trained models, making learned representations central to its explanation.
icml-2026-understanding-generalization-f.tldr: A post-training generalization bound connects embedding dimension and prediction sensitivity to the gap between held-out and population risk.

paragraphs: Semantic typography reshapes a character so that its appearance expresses a word’s meaning while remaining readable. Existing vector-based optimization methods can struggle to add concrete semantic detail and can distort the character’s structure. Intersections within the resulting glyph can further damage both legibility and visual quality.

VecDesigner introduces visual guidance into score distillation by using reference images related to the input text. These images provide more concrete cues for the desired semantic appearance. To maintain the character’s overall form, the method adds a vector-based Procrustes loss that constrains deformation. It also constrains positional relationships among control points to mitigate unwanted intersections.

The resulting optimization jointly addresses expressiveness, overall shape preservation, and local geometric artifacts. Experiments report better semantic expression and structural preservation than existing methods, producing glyphs described as expressive and clearly legible. The contribution shows how visual references and explicit vector constraints can work together when a design must communicate meaning through deformation while retaining a recognizable character.
icml-2026-vecdesigner-exploring-visual-g.tldr: VecDesigner combines reference-image guidance with vector geometry constraints to create expressive semantic typography that remains legible.
